transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. My kitchen table is just covered with things—my husband’s appointment papers, flyers from church, notes from the senior center, and these half-finished lists I keep making. I just sit there looking at it all, not knowing which thing to do first, and before I know it, the whole day is gone.
Do you find it difficult or distressing to throw these papers and flyers away?

No, it's not that I'm attached to them or afraid to throw them away. It's just... I can't seem to organize them. I know most of it is junk and needs to go in the trash, but the thought of actually going through the pile and sorting what to keep and what to toss just feels overwhelming. So it just sits there.
Has managing and organizing tasks always been a struggle for you throughout your life, or is this a recent change from how you used to be?

It has really been a struggle my whole life, not just recently. Even when I was a little girl... my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework. They constantly had to give me reminders to just finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside. So, yes, it has always been this way for me.
